To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) human skin wash extract (HSWE) and its fractions are attractive to female Aedes a.egypti; (2) the active fractions are composed of several different chemical compounds; (3) these compounds are perceived as different odour qualities by different receptor cells in the antennae of female A. aegyptio; and (4) the perception of the complex mixture HSWE is based on an integration of the individual responses of several receptor cells.

the olfactory receptor cells of A. aegypt are tuned to a wide variety of host odour components, and that the responses to a complex mixture of these components are the result of a complex across-fibre pattern of responses.

human skin wash extracts and its active chromatographic fractions, when applied to the antenna of female yellow fever mosquitoes, evoke across-fibre pattern responses in the antennal olfactory receptor neurons of the sensilla.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the sensory mechanisms of host finding and host selection of the yellow fever mosquito.
the question of how the female mosquito Aedes aegispti is able to detect and discriminate between the complex odour mixtures that are characteristic for its human host.
the question whether the mosquito's olfactory system is able to perceive the chemical composition of complex odour blends and to extract information on the identity of the source.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a complex pattern of odours is encoded by a complex pattern of responses in the olfactory system of the mosquito.

the olfactory receptors of female A. aegypt are able to recognize the human host odours and their components, but it is not clear whether this is the only or the main mechanism of host finding in the mosquito.

the olfactory system of female A. aegyptii can detect the human body odour in a complex pattern mode and that the pattern is composed of at least two major fractions which are both necessary to evoke the complete behavioural response.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the A3-type olfactory receptor neurons in Ae. aegyptii antennae respond to a complex mixture of human body odour components by generating a complex across-fibre pattern response.
the A3-type olfactory receptors in Aedes aegpti are able to detect a broad range of host-related odour compounds and are therefore well equipped to perceive the host odour in its complexity.

the antennal olfactory system of female Aedes aeygpti is able to detect a variety of compounds which may be involved in the perception of human body odours and which may contribute to the host-seeking behaviour.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we have shown that the antennal olfactory system of Aedes aegypii is capable of detecting a complex mixture of human body odour compounds and that the response to such a mixture can be described by the across-fibre pattern.
the olfactory system of the yellow fever mosquito has a remarkable ability to discriminate between different host odours and to recognize the presence of a human body in the vicinity of the mosquito.
the olfactory system of the yellow fever mosquito is capable of perceiving and decoding complex odour mixtures.
